items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: There was a guy in New York named Henry Williams(?), and I had heard him play, boy, and he had the most gorgeous tone I'd heard on saxophone.

ctx.x: See, how I got to Jacobson... There was a guy in New York named Henry Williams(?), and I had heard him play, boy, and he had the most gorgeous tone I'd heard on saxophone. And I heard...I don't know... I was checking some of the New York scene. I found out that he'd studied from a guy in Boston named Jacobson. And we was always going to Boston. So the next time I went to Boston, I looked up Jacobson, made an appointment with him on Friday, took my first lesson -- and boy, he shook me up so much and showed me so…
And he told me that he invented subtones, and I kind of I halfway believed him. Because he played subtones on clarinet, alto, anything he picked up...
